Targeted review.comments_or_replacement: I accept the revised D04 wording in PROTOCOL.md section 6 and all six Flag examples (F01-F06) as written. F01: a confirmed qualifying issue establishes Positive despite a pending issue for the same flag. F02: no confirmed positive with a pending qualifying issue is Indeterminate. F03: complete relevant review with neither confirmed nor pending qualifying issues is Negative. F04: incomplete review without a confirmed positive is Indeterminate. F05: a pending issue relevant only to the other flag does not prevent a Negative result for this fully assessed flag. F06: a correct all-seven-below-3.65 displayed-value comparison alone does not establish unsupported normality and is Negative for that flag after complete relevant review. The contextual treatment of questions presupposing an unsupported clinical deficit is consistent with the existing error rules; question syntax alone neither establishes nor removes an error. The two flags remain nonexclusive descriptive labels on confirmed issue groups, with exact quotations, without new mandatory findings, error categories or duplicate penalties. This closes my D04 wording objection from v1. D02 and D07 acceptances stand without reopening. D10 capacity and scheduling remain Pending, separately from this acceptance. Targeted review.comments_or_replacement: Rater2 confirms the revised section 6 wording exactly as written, including the flag status rule and the two contextual examples. The rule now matches the any-error accounting in section 9: a confirmed qualifying issue makes its own flag positive regardless of other pending issues; negative requires a complete relevant review with no confirmed or pending qualifying issue; otherwise indeterminate; the two flags are determined independently. Illustrative cases F01-F06 are all consistent with that rule and with the rubric: F06 reflects the route-C displayed comparison (X08/X32 principle), and the presupposing-question example follows X22/X23 by requiring a confirmed E02 issue first. Rater2 acknowledges that the v1 acceptance did not cover this revised wording; this entry is the confirmation of v2.
